findings.title: Member routes for add/remove not scoped to a specific group id
findings.body: The new routes `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` are declared inside `resources :groups do ... end` as collection-level routes (not `member do ... end`), producing paths like `/admin/groups/members` instead of `/admin/groups/:group_id/members`. The controller actions rely on `params.require(:group_id)` passed in the body/query instead of the URL, which works but is inconsistent with REST conventions used elsewhere in this file (e.g., `/users/:username/groups/:group_id`), and means the group id is not validated as part of the route, making CSRF-style/method confusion or missing-param errors less obvious. This is a design inconsistency rather than a crash, but it diverges from the rest of the routes file and could confuse future API consumers expecting `/admin/groups/:id/members`.

findings.title: members endpoint always issues two queries, no caching, breaking automatic/large group handling
findings.body: The previous implementation had special-case handling for automatic groups (limiting/offsetting large automatic groups to avoid timeouts/truncation issues) with a TODO about more than 200 groups truncating. The rewritten `members` action removes that special case and always does `group.users.count` plus a paginated query for every group type with a default limit of 50. For very large automatic groups (e.g. trust_level groups with tens of thousands of members) this now always executes a full COUNT(*) on every request, which can be an expensive query under load, especially since this is a public user-facing endpoint (`GroupsController`), not admin-only. There's no caching of the total count, which was presumably one of the reasons the former code treated automatic groups specially.

findings.title: findMembers silently returns undefined instead of a resolved promise when name is empty
findings.body: `findMembers` early-returns `undefined` (via bare `return ;`) when `name` is empty, whereas the previous code returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. Any caller doing `.then()` on the result of `findMembers()` (e.g. route hooks that previously chained promises) will now throw a TypeError if name happens to be empty, since `undefined` has no `.then` method. Although current call sites in this PR don't chain on this specific case, this is a behavior regression that silently breaks the promise contract of the function.

findings.title: addMembers never clears the input field after adding, acknowledged by stale TODO
findings.body: The `addMembers` action contains a TODO: "should clear the input" but it's left unaddressed. After adding members, the `usernames` property is not reset, so the user-selector field keeps showing the previously entered usernames, which is confusing when the admin wants to add another batch of members.

findings.title: members iterated in group.hbs but never defined for the new group (create) flow
findings.body: The template references `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` and `user_count`, which are populated only after `model.findMembers()` succeeds (triggered from the route). For a new group (no `id` yet), `{{#if id}}` guards the whole members+add-members block so this is fine, but once a group is saved for the first time via `create()`, `members`/`user_count`/`offset`/`limit` are never populated (findMembers is only called from the route's `setupController`, not after `create()`). This means immediately after creating a group and transitioning to `showGroup`, the newly created group's member section will render with stale/undefined pagination data until the admin navigates away and back, since `admin_group_route.js`'s `model` hook just looks up the already-cached group object rather than re-fetching it with members.
